anomalies.observed: The AVR-ISP-6 connector pin 1, labelled MISO, is connected to the PWM net together with MCU pins U2.6 and U3.6 (PB1), R2 (base drive to Q2), and R5 (fan PWM output). The ATtiny MISO-capable pins U2.2 and U3.2 (PB3) are instead connected to the POT net and not to J4.1.
anomalies.expected: For a standard AVR-ISP-6 programming header, pin 1 MISO should be connected to the ATtiny hardware SPI MISO pins, PB3 on U2.2/U3.2, on a separate MISO net rather than to the PWM/base-drive net.
anomalies.impact: Standard ISP programming would not work correctly because the programmer's MISO input is not connected to the MCU MISO pin. It instead sees the PWM signal and is tied to the fan PWM and transistor base-drive circuitry, which can prevent programming and may cause signal contention on the PWM line.
